STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast side of cooked bacon on a plate, photographed from directly overhead.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish side plate, about 22 cm wide. Its area is roughly 22 x 22 x 0.9 ≈ 435 cm^2, allowing for the rounded corners.

STEP 3 - Items: Crispy cooked bacon strips. One strip is on the right, and two or three overlapping or folded strips are in the center.

STEP 4 - Area: The right strip is about 12 cm long and 2 cm wide, so about 20 cm^2 (~5%). The center cluster covers about 60 cm^2 (~14%). Total is about 19% of the plate, so the food covers a small share of it.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon is thin, about 0.3 cm, but the center cluster is folded and overlapping, so I use 0.5 cm there. Right strip: 20 x 0.3 = 6 ml. Center: 60 x 0.5 = 30 ml. Total is 36 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bulk density is about 0.5, because the bacon is crispy and has gaps, and cooked bacon is light. 36 x 0.5 = 18 g. This matches about 3 to 4 cooked slices at roughly 4-5 g each.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked crispy bacon is about 540 kcal per 100 g. 18 g gives about 97 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 3 slices of bacon weighing 18 g and 97 kcal is plausible.
